record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Classify all finite connected geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane with exactly three unbalanced vertices; such a multinet is a finite connected multigraph in R^2 whose edges are straight-line segments with positive integer multiplicities, whose edges may intersect or self-intersect, whose balanced vertices satisfy the multiplicity-weighted zero-sum tangent condition, with degree-2 balanced vertices suppressed and no edge having both endpoints unbalanced.

evidence.quote: Our final convention is that we are going to consider here only connected geodesic (multi)nets
Problem 3.1.5. Classify all geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane with 3 unbalanced vertices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A *geodesic multinet* is a finite connected multigraph embedded in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose edges are straight-line segments, each carrying a positive integer multiplicity. Edges are allowed to intersect or self-intersect (intersection points that are not vertices are ignored). A vertex $v$ of the multinet is called *balanced* if 
$$\sum_{e \ni v} m(e)\, \mathbf{u}_e(v) = \mathbf{0},$$
where the sum is over all edges $e$ incident to $v$, $m(e)$ is the multiplicity of $e$, and $\mathbf{u}_e(v)$ is the unit tangent vector at $v$ pointing along $e$; otherwise $v$ is called *unbalanced*. The following normalizations are imposed:
(i) balanced vertices of degree $2$ are suppressed (i.e., no degree-$2$ balanced vertex is allowed);
(ii) no edge has both endpoints unbalanced.

Classify, up to similarity of $\mathbb{R}^2$, all finite connected geodesic multinets having exactly three unbalanced vertices.
artifact.status_search_result: For ordinary geodesic nets (all multiplicities equal to 1) with three unbalanced vertices in the Euclidean plane, the classification is known: the only such net consists of three segments joining each unbalanced vertex to the Fermat point of the triangle they form (Parsch, JDG 2021; arXiv:1803.03728). A more general result shows that in any non-positively curved Riemannian metric on the plane, a geodesic net with three unbalanced vertices has at most one balanced vertex. However, the classification question for geodesic multinets (allowing edge multiplicities) with three unbalanced vertices is still being studied, with recent works (e.g., arXiv:2412.02872, arXiv:2511.07810) extending balanced-vertex constructions but not delivering a complete classification in the multinet setting.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: A geodesic net with 3 unbalanced vertices A1,A2,A3 in the Euclidean plane has exactly one balanced vertex F at the Fermat point of A1,A2,A3 and three edges FAi.
status_evidence.claim: Classification solved for ordinary geodesic nets (multiplicities all 1) with three unbalanced vertices in the Euclidean plane.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of a balanced vertex in geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Each geodesic net with three unbalanced vertices on the plane endowed with a Riemannian metric of non-positive curvature has at most one balanced vertex.
status_evidence.claim: Recent ongoing research extends results on geodesic nets with three unbalanced vertices, indicating the multinet classification remains open.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of geodesic nets with prescribed numbers of unbalanced and balanced vertices.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent work on classifying/constructing geodesic (multi)nets; full multinet classification with three unbalanced vertices is not stated as solved.
